question: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised with effect from 1st January, _______.
solution:
The correct answer is **'1949'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised with effect from **1st ****January**** 1949** on the basis of the Reserve Bank of India (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
 
• All shares in the capital of the Bank were deemed transferred to the Central Government on payment of a suitable compensation.
 
• It commenced its operations on 1 April 1935 in accordance with the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The original share capital was divided into shares of 100 each fully paid. Following India's independence on 15 August 1947, the RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Imperial Bank of India was later nationalised in **1955 **and was named The State Bank of India, which is currently the largest Public sector Bank.
 
• The RBI supervises and regulates the **entire financial system**.
 
• This **boosts public confidence **in the nation's financial system, safeguards interest rates, and gives people good banking options.
 
• The main responsibility of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, the nation's central bank, is to oversee and direct the nation's financial system.
 
• It was founded in **1935 **as a legislative entity by the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The **Indian rupee's issuance **and supply are controlled by the central bank.
